architecture_findings.finding: At pinned Project-Frankenstein commit abba90a5767d85abc8a1ac340bae92842dab35c1, agentic/executor.py performs a causally pre-execution risk/approval check: when approval is required and skip_approval is false, execute() returns approval_required instead of dispatching the tool.

The historical AgentLoop separates a fixed safe-tool allowlist from all other tools. Safe tools execute with skip_approval=True; non-safe tools enter request_approval/wait_for_approval and only execute after approval. User denial returns a failed ToolResult without invoking the tool.

The historical executor also has independent pre-execution hard guards and optional Firejail restrictions. Deletion-pattern guards can stop Python/bash execution even after caller-side approval routing; if Firejail is absent, the source explicitly continues unsandboxed, so sandbox presence was not itself fail-closed authority.

The later current donor stern.py EffectGate is not a consolidation of the same enforcement semantics. Its generic Phase-2 zulassen() path explicitly never blocks tools and instead records admission/bookkeeping states. The effect lineage therefore contains a semantic split: historical caller-side enforcement -> later hook-side nonblocking admission/journal plus post-effect verification.

The first accessible git history entry for gschaidergabriel/frankenstein path scripts/stern.py is b0be33fb6b223cd0a34f0fabc00b71dc57c5cb6a on 2026-08-25; that snapshot already contains the Phase-2 two-sided EffectGate section. Querying the path before 2026-08-25 returned no commits. Therefore an exact posttool-only -> Phase-2 transition cannot be reconstructed from that public path history alone and must not be fabricated from comments.

The exact wache-koenig.py blocking predecessor referenced by current stern.py was not found in the inspected current Frankenstein tree or pinned Project-Frankenstein tree. Its existence as a historical external mechanism is source-referenced but its exact bytes, commit identity and runtime wiring remain unresolved.

frankenstein_2_effect_lineage_fusion.law: Do not choose between the historical pre-execution gate and the current post-effect verifier. Frankenstein-2.0 needs both, separated into typed causal states with one deterministic real-effect authority.
required_chain: EffectRequest(tool_use_id, session_id, generation, causal_event_id, request_digest, capability_scope)
EffectEnforcementReceipt proving DENY => no execution and ALLOW => exactly the admitted request may execute
CompletionEvidence accepted only from explicit verified admissible states
EffectJournal append-only causal chain; no mutable session-global current effect pointer and no caller boolean can mint authority
historical_parts_to_salvage: human approval event as a separate state
current_donor_parts_to_salvage: effect journaling and causal episode re-entry
parts_to_retire_or_replace: nonblocking ABGELEHNT state presented under an EffectGate name
mutable active_turns.effect_id as cross-hook correlation authority
completion predicates that accept ambiguous/failed/unverified effect statuses

preserved_contradictions.claim_b: Current stern.py generic EffectGate path intentionally does not block ordinary tool execution.
preserved_contradictions.resolution: Treat them as distinct architectural lineages and fuse their useful primitives behind canonical EntityOS EffectGate/EffectJournal rather than declaring either one-to-one inherited authority.
